from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Smoothie Metaphor (The Hook)", [
            "A smoothie is a blend of different ingredients.",
            "Complex signals are blends of simple sine waves.",
            "The Fourier Transform acts like a mathematical prism.",
            "It separates a combined signal into constituent parts.",
            "This reveals the hidden recipe of our reality."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Simple smoothie icon
        cup = Polygon(
            [-0.5, -0.8, 0], [0.5, -0.8, 0], [0.7, 0.8, 0], [-0.7, 0.8, 0],
            color=WHITE, stroke_width=2
        )
        liquid_top = cup.copy().set_stroke(width=0).set_fill(color="#FFC0CB", opacity=0.8).scale(0.9)
        liquid_bottom = cup.copy().set_stroke(width=0).set_fill(color="#FFFF00", opacity=0.8).scale(0.9).shift(DOWN*0.1)
        smoothie = VGroup(liquid_bottom, liquid_top, cup)
        
        self.place_in_area(smoothie, 'B3', 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(smoothie))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Split smoothie into components
        banana = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FFFFE0", fill_opacity=1)
        strawberry = Triangle(color="#FF9999", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.3)
        milk = RoundedRectangle(height=0.6, width=0.4, corner_radius=0.1, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1)
        
        banana_label = Text("Banana", font_size=16, color="#FFFFE0")
        strawberry_label = Text("Strawberry", font_size=16, color="#FF9999")
        milk_label = Text("Milk", font_size=16, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        banana_grp = VGroup(banana, banana_label.next_to(banana, DOWN, buff=0.1))
        strawberry_grp = VGroup(strawberry, strawberry_label.next_to(strawberry, DOWN, buff=0.1))
        milk_grp = VGroup(milk, milk_label.next_to(milk, DOWN, buff=0.1))
        
        ingredients = VGroup(banana_grp, strawberry_grp, milk_grp).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(ingredients, 'B1', 'B6')
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(smoothie),
            FadeIn(ingredients)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Replace with complex wave
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5], x_length=5, y_length=2).set_opacity(0)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B1', 'C6')
        
        # Frequencies for the 3 components
        complex_wave = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 0.6*np.sin(2*PI*0.5*x) + 0.3*np.sin(2*PI*1.5*x) + 0.2*np.sin(2*PI*3*x),
            color=WHITE
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(ingredients),
            Create(complex_wave)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        prism = Polygon(
            [-0.7, -0.6, 0], [0.7, -0.6, 0], [0, 0.8, 0],
            color="#ADD8E6", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2
        )
        self.place_in_area(prism, 'D3', 'D4')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(prism))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Decomposed waves
        axes_b1 = Axes(x_range=[0, 4], y_range=[-1, 1], x_length=1.5, y_length=1).set_opacity(0)
        axes_b2 = axes_b1.copy()
        axes_b3 = axes_b1.copy()
        
        wave1 = axes_b1.plot(lambda x: 0.7*np.sin(2*PI*0.5*x), color="#FFFFE0")
        wave2 = axes_b2.plot(lambda x: 0.5*np.sin(2*PI*1.5*x), color="#FF9999")
        wave3 = axes_b3.plot(lambda x: 0.3*np.sin(2*PI*3*x), color="#FFFFFF")
        
        waves_grp = VGroup(
            VGroup(axes_b1, wave1),
            VGroup(axes_b2, wave2),
            VGroup(axes_b3, wave3)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(waves_grp, 'F1', 'F6')
        
        # Animate "passing through"
        self.play(
            complex_wave.animate.scale(0.3).move_to(prism.get_center()),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            FadeOut(complex_wave),
            Create(waves_grp)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        time_label = Text("Time Domain", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        freq_label = Text("Frequency Domain", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_in_area(time_label, 'A1', 'A6')
        self.place_in_area(freq_label, 'E1', 'E6')
        
        self.play(Write(time_label), Write(freq_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Prerequisites: The DNA of Waves"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Every complex wave consists of simple sine waves.",
            "- Amplitude determines the wave's height or volume.",
            "- Frequency measures how fast the wave oscillates.",
            "- Phase indicates the wave's starting position.",
            "- Circular motion generates periodic oscillations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_COMPLEX = WHITE
        COLOR_AMP = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_FREQ = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_PHASE = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_CIRC = "#FFFF00"

        # Shared Axes for wave property demos
        ax = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 2*PI, PI/2], 
            y_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1], 
            x_length=4.5, 
            y_length=3.5, 
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).set_stroke(opacity=0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Every complex wave consists of simple sine waves.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_COMPLEX)
        self.place_in_area(ax, 'B2', 'E6')
        
        def wave1(x): return np.sin(x)
        def wave2(x): return 0.5 * np.sin(3*x)
        def wave3(x): return 0.3 * np.sin(5*x)
        def complex_wave_func(x): return wave1(x) + wave2(x) + wave3(x)

        comp_plot = ax.plot(complex_wave_func, color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(ax), Create(comp_plot))
        self.wait(0.5)

        w1_plot = ax.plot(wave1, color=WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.4)
        w2_plot = ax.plot(wave2, color=WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.4)
        w3_plot = ax.plot(wave3, color=WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(comp_plot.copy(), w1_plot),
            ReplacementTransform(comp_plot.copy(), w2_plot),
            ReplacementTransform(comp_plot.copy(), w3_plot),
            comp_plot.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.15)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(w1_plot, w2_plot, w3_plot, comp_plot))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Amplitude determines the wave's height or volume.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_AMP)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        amp_sine = always_redraw(lambda: ax.plot(lambda x: amp_tracker.get_value() * np.sin(x), color=COLOR_AMP))
        amp_label = Text("Amplitude", font_size=24, color=COLOR_AMP)
        self.place_at_grid(amp_label, 'B4')
        
        self.play(Create(amp_sine), Write(amp_label))
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=1)
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(0.4), run_time=1)
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(amp_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Frequency measures how fast the wave oscillates.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_FREQ)
        freq_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        freq_sine = always_redraw(lambda: ax.plot(lambda x: np.sin(freq_tracker.get_value() * x), color=COLOR_FREQ))
        freq_label = Text("Frequency", font_size=24, color=COLOR_FREQ)
        self.place_at_grid(freq_label, 'B4')
        
        self.play(FadeOut(amp_sine), Create(freq_sine), Write(freq_label))
        self.play(freq_tracker.animate.set_value(3.5), run_time=1)
        self.play(freq_tracker.animate.set_value(0.6), run_time=1)
        self.play(freq_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(freq_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Phase indicates the wave's starting position.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_PHASE)
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0.0)
        
        phase_sine = always_redraw(lambda: ax.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x + phase_tracker.get_value()), color=COLOR_PHASE))
        phase_label = Text("Phase", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PHASE)
        self.place_at_grid(phase_label, 'B4')
        
        self.play(FadeOut(freq_sine), Create(phase_sine), Write(phase_label))
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=1)
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(-PI), run_time=1)
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(phase_sine, phase_label, ax))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Circular motion generates periodic oscillations.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_CIRC)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=0.9, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'D2')
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        dot = Dot(color=COLOR_CIRC)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(circle.get_center() + np.array([0.9*np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0.9*np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0])))
        
        arm = always_redraw(lambda: Line(circle.get_center(), dot.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2))
        
        wave_ax = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 2*PI, PI/2], 
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], 
            x_length=3.5, 
            y_length=2.5, 
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(wave_ax, 'D3', 'D6')
        
        drawing_sine = always_redraw(lambda: wave_ax.plot(
            lambda x: np.sin(x), 
            x_range=[0, max(0.001, angle_tracker.get_value())], 
            color=WHITE
        ))
        
        horizontal_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            dot.get_center(), 
            wave_ax.c2p(angle_tracker.get_value(), np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value())), 
            color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=1
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(dot), Create(arm), Create(wave_ax))
        self.add(horizontal_line, drawing_sine)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2*PI), run_time=6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain", [
            "- Time domain shows signals changing over time.",
            "- Frequency domain reveals the individual frequencies present.",
            "- Fourier Transform bridges these two distinct perspectives."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A messy magenta signal wave (#FF00FF) oscillates in a 2D time-plot.
        
        axes_time = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": True},
            tips=False
        )
        time_label = Text("Time", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        amp_label = Text("Amp", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        
        # Wave: Sum of 3 sines to look "messy"
        wave = axes_time.plot(
            lambda t: np.sin(2 * PI * 1 * t) + 0.5 * np.sin(2 * PI * 3 * t) + 0.2 * np.sin(2 * PI * 5 * t),
            color="#FF00FF",
            x_range=[0, 4]
        )
        
        plot_group_time = VGroup(axes_time, wave)
        self.place_in_area(plot_group_time, 'B1', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Label positioning
        self.place_at_grid(time_label, 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(amp_label, 'B1', scale_factor=0.8)
        time_label.shift(DOWN * 0.3 + RIGHT * 0.3)
        amp_label.shift(UP * 0.3 + LEFT * 0.3)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Create(axes_time), Create(wave), Write(time_label), Write(amp_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The view rotates 90 degrees to show three sharp yellow spikes (#FFFF00) on a frequency-axis.
        
        axes_freq = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": True},
            tips=False
        )
        freq_label = Text("Frequency", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        mag_label = Text("Mag", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        
        # Spikes at 1, 3, 5 corresponding to the sines used in the wave
        s1 = Line(axes_freq.c2p(1, 0), axes_freq.c2p(1, 1), color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        s2 = Line(axes_freq.c2p(3, 0), axes_freq.c2p(3, 0.5), color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        s3 = Line(axes_freq.c2p(5, 0), axes_freq.c2p(5, 0.2), color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        spikes = VGroup(s1, s2, s3)
        
        plot_group_freq = VGroup(axes_freq, spikes)
        self.place_in_area(plot_group_freq, 'B1', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(freq_label, 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(mag_label, 'B1', scale_factor=0.8)
        freq_label.shift(DOWN * 0.3 + RIGHT * 0.3)
        mag_label.shift(UP * 0.3 + LEFT * 0.3)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Simulated rotation/perspective shift via Transform
        # Use a slight scale change during transform to suggest depth shift
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(wave, spikes),
            ReplacementTransform(axes_time, axes_freq),
            ReplacementTransform(time_label, freq_label),
            ReplacementTransform(amp_label, mag_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A cyan double-headed arrow (#00FFFF) pulses between the time-wave and the frequency-spikes.
        
        arrow = DoubleArrow(
            start=self.grid['F2'],
            end=self.grid['F5'],
            color="#00FFFF",
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        ft_text = Text("Fourier Transform", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(ft_text, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        ft_text.shift(UP * 0.3 + RIGHT * 0.5)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(arrow), Write(ft_text))
        
        # Pulse the arrow to emphasize the bridge
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(arrow.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.4, rate_func=there_and_back)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Mechanism: The Winding Machine",
            [
                "We can wrap a signal around a circular path.",
                "Most winding speeds create a balanced, centered shape.",
                "When speeds match, the shape becomes unbalanced.",
                "The center of mass shifts away from origin.",
                "This peak identifies a frequency within the signal."
            ]
        )

        # Center point of the winding machine
        center_pos = self.grid["C4"] + np.array([0.5, -0.5, 0]) # Approximately center of B2-E5
        
        # Constants
        SIGNAL_FREQ = 1.0
        T_MAX = 4.0
        
        # Trackers
        wind_freq_tracker = ValueTracker(0.4)
        
        # Helper function for winding
        def get_wound_point(t, wind_freq):
            # s(t) = 1.5 + cos(2 * pi * f_sig * t)
            # x = s(t) * cos(-2 * pi * f_wind * t)
            # y = s(t) * sin(-2 * pi * f_wind * t)
            radius = 1.2 + 0.6 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * SIGNAL_FREQ * t)
            angle = -2 * np.pi * wind_freq * t
            return center_pos + np.array([radius * np.cos(angle), radius * np.sin(angle), 0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "We can wrap a signal around a circular path."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        origin_dot = Dot(center_pos, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.add(origin_dot)
        
        # Initial wound shape
        wound_shape = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: get_wound_point(t, wind_freq_tracker.get_value()),
            t_range=[0, T_MAX],
            color="#00FF00"
        )
        
        self.play(Create(wound_shape), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Most winding speeds create a balanced, centered shape."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show that it's balanced at 0.4
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "When speeds match, the shape becomes unbalanced."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Add center of mass dot
        def get_cm():
            points = [get_wound_point(t, wind_freq_tracker.get_value()) for t in np.linspace(0, T_MAX, 100)]
            return np.mean(points, axis=0)

        cm_dot = Dot(get_cm(), color="#FF0000")
        cm_label = Text("Center of Mass", font_size=16, color="#FF0000")
        # Position label near CM (grid D5 approx)
        self.place_at_grid(cm_label, "E5")
        
        # Add updater to shape and dot
        wound_shape.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            ParametricFunction(
                lambda t: get_wound_point(t, wind_freq_tracker.get_value()),
                t_range=[0, T_MAX],
                color="#00FF00"
            )
        ))
        
        cm_dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_cm()))

        self.play(FadeIn(cm_dot), Write(cm_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition freq to matching freq 1.0
        self.play(
            wind_freq_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "The center of mass shifts away from origin."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Shift is already visible, maybe add an arrow
        arrow = Arrow(origin_dot.get_center(), cm_dot.get_center(), color="#FF0000", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This peak identifies a frequency within the signal."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Cleanup updaters
        wound_shape.clear_updaters()
        cm_dot.clear_updaters()
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title_text = "Practical Magic: Noise Cancellation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Noise appears as unwanted spikes in frequency.",
            "Setting these specific spikes to zero removes noise.",
            "Transforming back results in a clean, clear signal."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors as per storyboard and matching requirement
        VOICE_COLOR = "#00FF00"  # Green
        NOISE_COLOR = "#FF0000"  # Red
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1 focus: Noise (Red)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(NOISE_COLOR)
        
        # Time domain axes in top area
        ax_time = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": BLUE_D},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=2.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(ax_time, "A1", "C6")
        time_label = Text("Time Domain Signal", font_size=18).next_to(ax_time, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Create voice (green) and noise (red) waves
        # Frequency 0.5 Hz for voice, 5 Hz for noise
        voice_wave = ax_time.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * 0.5 * x), color=VOICE_COLOR)
        noise_wave = ax_time.plot(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 5 * x), color=NOISE_COLOR)
        
        self.play(Create(ax_time), Write(time_label))
        self.play(Create(voice_wave), Create(noise_wave), run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Combine them into a single white signal
        combined_wave = ax_time.plot(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * 0.5 * x) + 0.3 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 5 * x), 
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(voice_wave, noise_wave), combined_wave),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2 focus: Noise Removal (Red)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(NOISE_COLOR)
        
        # Frequency domain axes in bottom area
        ax_freq = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 8, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": BLUE_D},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=2.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(ax_freq, "D1", "F6")
        freq_label = Text("Frequency Spectrum", font_size=18).next_to(ax_freq, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Frequency spikes corresponding to the time-domain components
        voice_spike = Line(
            ax_freq.c2p(0.5, 0), ax_freq.c2p(0.5, 1.0), 
            color=VOICE_COLOR, stroke_width=6
        )
        noise_spike = Line(
            ax_freq.c2p(5.0, 0), ax_freq.c2p(5.0, 0.3), 
            color=NOISE_COLOR, stroke_width=6
        )
        
        self.play(Create(ax_freq), Write(freq_label))
        self.play(GrowFromEdge(voice_spike, DOWN), GrowFromEdge(noise_spike, DOWN))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Demonstrate noise cancellation by zeroing the noise spike
        self.play(noise_spike.animate.scale(0.001, about_edge=DOWN), run_time=1.5)
        self.remove(noise_spike)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3 focus: Clean Signal (Green)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(VOICE_COLOR)
        
        # Show the result of filtering in the time domain
        clean_voice_wave = ax_time.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * 0.5 * x), color=VOICE_COLOR)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(combined_wave, clean_voice_wave),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Teaching script and title
        lecture_lines = [
            "Fourier Transforms power modern digital technology.",
            "They enable efficient data compression for JPEGs.",
            "This tool is the foundation of digital communication."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Digital Impact", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Cyan icons (#00FFFF) for MP3, JPEG, and Wi-Fi float around a prism.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CYAN)
        
        prism = Triangle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1).scale(1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(prism, "C3", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        icon_mp3 = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(height=0.6, width=1.1, color=CYAN), 
            Text("MP3", font_size=18, color=CYAN)
        )
        icon_jpeg = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(height=0.6, width=1.1, color=CYAN), 
            Text("JPEG", font_size=18, color=CYAN)
        )
        icon_wifi = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(height=0.6, width=1.1, color=CYAN), 
            Text("Wi-Fi", font_size=18, color=CYAN)
        )
        
        self.place_at_grid(icon_mp3, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(icon_jpeg, "A5")
        self.place_at_grid(icon_wifi, "B1")
        
        # Persistent mobjects for floating effect
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        self.add(time_tracker)
        time_tracker.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.increment_value(dt))
        
        # Save base positions for oscillating update
        pos_mp3 = icon_mp3.get_center().copy()
        pos_jpeg = icon_jpeg.get_center().copy()
        pos_wifi = icon_wifi.get_center().copy()
        
        icon_mp3.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(pos_mp3 + UP * 0.15 * np.sin(time_tracker.get_value() * 2)))
        icon_jpeg.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(pos_jpeg + DOWN * 0.15 * np.cos(time_tracker.get_value() * 1.5)))
        icon_wifi.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(pos_wifi + RIGHT * 0.15 * np.sin(time_tracker.get_value() * 2.2)))
        
        self.play(Create(prism), FadeIn(icon_mp3), FadeIn(icon_jpeg), FadeIn(icon_wifi))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A large stack of data blocks shrinks into a single yellow byte icon (#FFFF00).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Representing raw data blocks
        blocks = VGroup(*[
            Square(side_length=0.3, fill_opacity=0.6, fill_color=GREY_A, stroke_width=1) 
            for _ in range(12)
        ])
        blocks.arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=4, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(blocks, "D1", "E3")
        
        byte_icon = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(height=0.7, width=0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.2), 
            Text("01", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(byte_icon, "E5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(blocks))
        self.wait(1)
        # Compression animation
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(blocks, byte_icon))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The title 'Fourier Transform: The Recipe of Reality' fades in for the finale.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        
        final_title = Text(
            "Fourier Transform:\nThe Recipe of Reality", 
            font_size=36, 
            color=WHITE_COLOR, 
            line_spacing=1.2
        )
        self.place_in_area(final_title, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Final sequence: Fade out distractions and show grand title
        self.play(
            FadeOut(prism), 
            FadeOut(icon_mp3), 
            FadeOut(icon_jpeg), 
            FadeOut(icon_wifi),
            FadeOut(byte_icon),
            FadeIn(final_title)
        )
        self.wait(5)

outline.topic: Fourier Transform: The Recipe of Reality
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM or curious learners with basic calculus knowledge

sections.title: The Smoothie Metaphor (The Hook)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of deconstruction. Just as a smoothie can be broken down into its original ingredients (bananas, strawberries, milk), a complex signal can be broken down into pure sine waves. Explain that the Fourier Transform is the mathematical 'prism' that separates a combined result into its constituent parts.
sections.example: An animated 'Sound Smoothie' machine: A DJ plays a chord. The Fourier Transform acts like a filter that pulls out three distinct fruits representing three different notes (frequencies).

sections.title: Prerequisites: The DNA of Waves
sections.content: Briefly review the Sine Wave. Emphasize three properties: Amplitude (how loud/tall), Frequency (how fast it oscillates), and Phase (where it starts). This is necessary because the Fourier Transform assumes every signal is just a sum of these simple waves.
sections.example: A visual of a rotating circle with a 'tracing arm' that draws a sine wave on a moving paper roll to show the relationship between circular motion and wave oscillation.

sections.title: Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain
sections.content: Introduce the two perspectives of looking at data. The 'Time Domain' (what we usually see, like an oscilloscope) and the 'Frequency Domain' (the Fourier view). Explain that the Fourier Transform is the bridge between these two 'views' of the same reality.
sections.example: A 3D perspective shift: Looking at a signal from the side shows a messy, tangled wave (Time). Rotating the view 90 degrees reveals clean, distinct spikes on a graph (Frequency).

sections.title: The Mechanism: The Winding Machine
sections.content: Explain the 'Winding' intuition. If you wrap a signal around a center point at a certain frequency, the 'center of mass' remains at the origin UNLESS the winding frequency matches a frequency present in the signal. When they match, the center of mass 'plucks' out or shifts away from the center.
sections.example: An animation of a string being wound around a spool. When the spool spins at the 'wrong' speed, the shape is a messy flower. When it hits the 'right' speed, the shape becomes unbalanced, indicating a detected frequency.

sections.title: Practical Magic: Noise Cancellation
sections.content: Demonstrate how the Fourier Transform allows us to manipulate signals. By identifying a specific frequency as 'noise,' we can set its amplitude to zero in the frequency domain and transform the signal back to time, resulting in a clean output.
sections.example: A character named 'Felix the Cat' is trying to sleep, but a fan is humming. We show the fan's 'hum' as a specific spike on the frequency graph. We 'click' the spike to delete it, and the room becomes silent.

sections.title: Summary and Digital Impact
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting that without the Fourier Transform, modern life (MP3s, JPEGs, Wi-Fi, and MRI scans) wouldn't exist. It is the ultimate tool for data compression and signal processing.
sections.example: A montage of a smartphone shrinking a giant stack of sheet music (raw data) into a tiny digital file (compressed data) using the Fourier 'Prism'.
